patient.context_label: ROS1-positive advanced NSCLC or separate eligible NTRK fusion-positive tumour
patient.scope_note: This adult suite covers entrectinib alone for ROS1-positive advanced NSCLC before any ROS1 inhibitor (00702a), or a separate NTRK gene-fusion solid-tumour indication with no previous NTRK inhibitor and no satisfactory treatment options (00702b). Molecular tests and Irish access criteria must be confirmed. The adult 600 mg schedule does not apply to children.
patient.schedule_label: Daily oral treatment without a rest week
patient.schedule_summary: The usual adult starting dose is 600 mg by mouth once daily, every day without a planned rest week. Use your prescribed dose. Treatment continues while helping and side effects remain acceptable; there is no fixed number of cycles.
patient.purpose: Entrectinib aims to control a cancer with a matching gene fusion. It may help shrink or slow cancer, including some cancer in the brain. Your team explains the treatment aim, uncertainty and alternatives for your exact setting.
patient.indication_text: This adult suite covers entrectinib alone for ROS1-positive advanced NSCLC before any ROS1 inhibitor (00702a), or a separate NTRK gene-fusion solid-tumour indication with no previous NTRK inhibitor and no satisfactory treatment options (00702b). Molecular tests and Irish access criteria must be confirmed. The adult 600 mg schedule does not apply to children.
patient.administration_text: Take whole capsules with or without food; do not crush or chew. Avoid grapefruit, grapefruit products and Seville oranges. If a dose is missed, take it unless the next dose is due within 12 hours; confirm the exact boundary with your pharmacist. The leaflet permits repeating whole capsules after immediate vomiting: follow your written plan and call if uncertain. Suspension or tube administration requires separate pharmacy instructions.
patient.monitoring_summary: Blood count, kidney/liver tests, uric acid and ECG/electrolytes before starting. Repeat ECG/electrolytes after one month, then periodically as indicated; regular blood tests and symptom reviews. Heart-pumping tests depend on symptoms/risk. Scans follow your Consultant’s plan. Confirm who arranges and reviews each check.

agents.name: Entrectinib
agents.mechanism: Blocks abnormal ROS1 or TRK growth signals
agents.explanation: Entrectinib inhibits proteins made by selected ROS1 or NTRK gene fusions. Blocking these signals can slow cancer growth. The relevant fusion, tumour setting and previous medicines determine eligibility; ROS1 and NTRK are different indications.
agents.watch: Report heart, thinking/memory, vision and bone symptoms early.
risks: Taste change, nausea, constipation or diarrhoea
Liver injury and low blood counts
Raised uric acid and kidney-test changes
Visual disturbance, nerve symptoms and fractures

logistics.title: Your practical treatment plan
logistics.intro: The usual adult starting dose is 600 mg by mouth once daily, every day without a planned rest week. Use your prescribed dose. Treatment continues while helping and side effects remain acceptable; there is no fixed number of cycles.

sections.title: Start with a clear plan
sections.text: Confirm the gene fusion, indication, dose, supply route, baseline tests, next review and urgent contact numbers.

sections.title: Whole capsules or another method
sections.text: Swallow whole capsules. If swallowing is difficult, contact pharmacy: current product information allows a specifically prepared suspension, while the older NCCP text says not to open capsules. Do not improvise.

sections.title: Supply and appointments
sections.text: Arrange repeat prescriptions before capsules run out. Oral treatment needs blood tests and heart reviews but no routine infusion line or pump.

sections.title: If a dose is missed or vomited
sections.text: Use the written missed-dose and immediate-vomiting instructions for your formulation. Ask the team if timing is unclear; suspension vomiting needs professional advice.

sections.title: If treatment changes
sections.text: Ask what must recover, who authorises restarting and when the next review is due. Continue follow-up and contraception advice after stopping.

evidence.title: Evidence depends on the gene fusion and tumour
evidence.intro: Separate studies found tumour shrinkage and periods of cancer control in ROS1-positive lung cancer and NTRK fusion-positive tumours, including some brain metastases. These studies generally had no randomised comparison group; they do not establish an individual survival benefit or superiority over other targeted medicines.
evidence.population: Adults with ROS1 TKI-naive advanced ROS1-positive NSCLC, or separate NTRK inhibitor-naive fusion-positive solid tumours.
evidence.interpretation: Separate studies found tumour shrinkage and periods of cancer control in ROS1-positive lung cancer and NTRK fusion-positive tumours, including some brain metastases. These studies generally had no randomised comparison group; they do not establish an individual survival benefit or superiority over other targeted medicines.
evidence.limitations: These group results cannot predict your outcome; other treatment options, prior medicines and tumour type matter.

patient.teachback: Explain your daily dose, what to do after a missed or vomited dose, which symptoms need a call, and who arranges your one-month ECG/electrolytes.
patient.consent_support: Discuss the exact ROS1 or NTRK indication, alternatives including not proceeding, expected benefit and uncertainty, cognitive/heart/liver risks, fractures, daily capsules, interactions, monitoring and reproductive precautions.

support.title: Symptom medicines
support.text: NCCP rates entrectinib minimal-to-low oral emetic risk. Agree individual rescue treatment and check heart-rhythm interactions; no routine infusion premedication is specified.

support.title: Daily life and medicines
support.text: Keep the medicine list current. Avoid driving or machinery while dizzy, faint, visually affected or cognitively affected. Review falls risk and report bone pain.

support.title: Pregnancy and breastfeeding
support.text: Use the agreed contraception plan during and after treatment. Do not breastfeed during treatment; ask about fertility and family plans before starting.

chapters.title: Your treatment setting
chapters.intro: Entrectinib aims to control a cancer with a matching gene fusion. It may help shrink or slow cancer, including some cancer in the brain. Your team explains the treatment aim, uncertainty and alternatives for your exact setting.

chapters.title: Before and during treatment
chapters.intro: Regular checks help find changes early.

items.title: Before the first dose
items.text: Before starting: confirm fusion, previous targeted treatment, access and pregnancy precautions; blood count, kidney/liver tests, uric acid, ECG/electrolytes and cognitive symptoms. Heart-pumping assessment is needed for heart-failure symptoms or risk; brain imaging follows the Consultant plan.

items.title: Ongoing reviews
items.text: During treatment: repeat blood count, kidney/liver tests and uric acid at agreed reviews. Repeat ECG/electrolytes after one month, then periodically as indicated. Assess thinking/memory, heart symptoms, vision and bone pain; scans follow the Consultant plan.

items.title: Whole capsules and missed doses
items.text: Take whole capsules with or without food; do not crush or chew. Avoid grapefruit, grapefruit products and Seville oranges. If a dose is missed, take it unless the next dose is due within 12 hours; confirm the exact boundary with your pharmacist. The leaflet permits repeating whole capsules after immediate vomiting: follow your written plan and call if uncertain. Suspension or tube administration requires separate pharmacy instructions.

items.title: Interactions
items.text: Give the team a complete medicine and supplement list, including St John’s wort. CYP3A inhibitors/inducers and medicines affecting heart rhythm need pharmacy review. Do not change the cancer dose yourself; temporary interaction doses differ from toxicity reductions.

items.title: Swallowing difficulty
items.text: Ask pharmacy for the approved method. Current SmPC allows capsule suspension and enteral administration; the older NCCP says not to open capsules. Instructions and vomiting advice depend on the formulation.

items.title: Thinking, vision and driving
items.text: Do not drive or use machinery while experiencing dizziness, fainting, blurred vision or cognitive effects. Ask family/supporters to report noticeable memory or behaviour changes.

items.title: Bones and falls
items.text: New focal pain, changed gait or mobility needs prompt review for a fracture; reduce fall hazards where possible.

items.title: Pregnancy, fertility and breastfeeding
items.text: Avoid pregnancy. Women who could become pregnant need highly effective contraception during treatment and for at least five weeks afterwards; add a barrier method if using systemic hormonal contraception. Men with partners who could become pregnant need highly effective contraception during treatment and for at least three months afterwards. Do not breastfeed during treatment. Discuss fertility and family plans before starting.

items.title: Support medicines
items.text: Use prescribed symptom treatment. No routine steroid, G-CSF or antimicrobial prophylaxis is specified for this monotherapy; avoid borrowing an infusion antiemetic schedule.

chapters.title: When to get help
chapters.intro: Do not wait for the next appointment.

items.title: Call urgently
items.text: Call the oncology team urgently for new or worsening breathlessness, swelling, palpitations or fainting; marked confusion or memory change; fever, jaundice, severe diarrhoea or inability to drink. Report new visual disturbance and focal bone pain promptly. Follow your unit’s temperature/contact instructions. Severe breathing difficulty, chest pain or collapse needs emergency help.

chapters.title: What studies can tell us
chapters.intro: Separate studies found tumour shrinkage and periods of cancer control in ROS1-positive lung cancer and NTRK fusion-positive tumours, including some brain metastases. These studies generally had no randomised comparison group; they do not establish an individual survival benefit or superiority over other targeted medicines.

items.title: Your decision
items.text: Ask how the correct molecular and tumour-specific study population compares with your situation. Study averages do not establish personal prognosis or rank current therapies.

chapters.title: When treatment changes
chapters.intro: Continuation and restart are clinical decisions.

items.title: Hold or stop
items.text: Ask why treatment is held, which tests or symptoms must recover, who will authorise restarting and what follow-up is needed.

key_points: Adult ROS1 00702a and NTRK 00702b have distinct eligibility/prior-inhibitor requirements.
Daily 600 mg starting dose; toxicity ladder 400/200 mg; no fixed course or rest week.
QTc 481–500 ms already requires hold; >500 ms has cause-dependent restart. Baseline >450 ms is an EMA avoidance criterion.
CHF, cognition, uric acid, liver injury and haematology have different recovery thresholds; no generic TKI algorithm.
Do not import permanent ILD stop or isolated CK dose thresholds from another TKI.
NCCP CTCAE v4.0, current SmPC formulation and interaction distinctions are explicit.

rationale.summary: Entrectinib aims to control a cancer with a matching gene fusion. It may help shrink or slow cancer, including some cancer in the brain. Your team explains the treatment aim, uncertainty and alternatives for your exact setting. This adult suite covers entrectinib alone for ROS1-positive advanced NSCLC before any ROS1 inhibitor (00702a), or a separate NTRK gene-fusion solid-tumour indication with no previous NTRK inhibitor and no satisfactory treatment options (00702b). Molecular tests and Irish access criteria must be confirmed. The adult 600 mg schedule does not apply to children.
rationale.setting: ROS1-positive advanced NSCLC or separate eligible NTRK fusion-positive tumour
rationale.line: ROS1 TKI-naive advanced NSCLC, or separate NTRK inhibitor-naive eligible solid tumours.
factors: Validated fusion, stage, previous inhibitors, satisfactory alternatives and MAP criteria.
Cardiac/QT, cognitive, hepatic and renal function, interactions, reproductive plans and patient priorities.
alternatives: Discuss current MDT-selected targeted therapies, other systemic options, trials and supportive care including not proceeding; no cross-trial ranking.
limitations: ROS1 and NTRK are separate molecular populations. Results are not transferable between them or to patients previously treated with the excluded targeted inhibitor.
The cited integrated studies were single-arm phase I/II cohorts; they cannot show head-to-head superiority or a causal survival gain.
The NTRK all-tumour result combines small and diverse tumour groups. The 2024 NTRK lung subset is separately labelled and should not be assigned to other tissues.

NCCP eligibility prints age >18 and lists CNS involvement for ROS1, while the broad adult indication/EMA licence do not require brain disease; clarify current MAP interpretation rather than inventing eligibility.
NCCP v2 capsule-opening restriction predates current SmPC suspension instructions; pharmacy must direct any alternative administration. Independent clinical, pharmacy and PPI review remains pending.

evidence.trial: ROS1 integrated analysis 2024; NTRK integrated analysis 2022 and NSCLC subset 2024
evidence.population: 172 adults with ROS1-positive advanced NSCLC; separately 121 adults with NTRK-positive diverse tumours and 51 with NTRK-positive NSCLC.
evidence.comparison: Entrectinib 600 mg orally daily; no randomised comparator in these analyses.
evidence.applicability: Separate studies found tumour shrinkage and periods of cancer control in ROS1-positive lung cancer and NTRK fusion-positive tumours, including some brain metastases. These studies generally had no randomised comparison group; they do not establish an individual survival benefit or superiority over other targeted medicines.

endpoints.interpretation: Fan 2024;  n=172, 116 responses; 95%CI 59.9–74.4. Data cutoff 2 August 2021, median survival follow-up 37.8 months. ROS 1 TKI-naive;  includes differing prior non-ROS 1 systemic treatment.
95%CI 12.2–22.4 at the same 2021 cutoff. PFS is not overall survival;  no comparative survival benefit can be inferred.

endpoints.metric: NTRK-positive solid tumours: BICR objective response
endpoints.interpretation: Demetri 2022; n=121, 14 tumour types; 74 responses. Cutoff 31 August 2020; median follow-up 25.8 months. Mixed-tissue response cannot be assigned to an individual tumour type.

endpoints.metric: NTRK-positive NSCLC only: BICR objective response
endpoints.interpretation: Cho 2024; n=51, 32 responses; 95%CI 48.1–75.9. Cutoff 2 August 2022; median survival follow-up 26.3 months. This is a separate NTRK lung cohort, not ROS 1 or a head-to-head comparison.

limitations: ROS1 and NTRK are separate molecular populations. Results are not transferable between them or to patients previously treated with the excluded targeted inhibitor.
The cited integrated studies were single-arm phase I/II cohorts; they cannot show head-to-head superiority or a causal survival gain.
The NTRK all-tumour result combines small and diverse tumour groups. The 2024 NTRK lung subset is separately labelled and should not be assigned to other tissues.

NCCP eligibility prints age >18 and lists CNS involvement for ROS1, while the broad adult indication/EMA licence do not require brain disease; clarify current MAP interpretation rather than inventing eligibility.
NCCP v2 capsule-opening restriction predates current SmPC suspension instructions; pharmacy must direct any alternative administration. Independent clinical, pharmacy and PPI review remains pending.
evidence.harms: Cognitive changes/dizziness, CHF/QT effects, fractures, uric acid and liver abnormalities, low blood counts, bowel effects, oedema/weight gain and visual changes require active review; treatment interruption or cessation may be needed.
